messages:
anya: heads-up — new starter sample fails type-check in edge runtime build when using our sdk ESM entry.
anya: local node/dev build (cjs interop) is fine, but when targeting edge (esmodule + strict) TS complains about overload resolution and 'unknown' inference.
anya: error snippet: `TS2345: Argument of type 'Request' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string | RequestInit'.` — comes from our client.request overloads.
devon: ugh. do you have a minimal repro? repo or paste of tsconfig?
anya: pasted the small repro below (using vite+esbuild edge target).
anya: ```tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "lib": ["ES2020", "DOM"],
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": false,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "types": ["node"]
  }
}
```
anya: and the snippet that trips it: ```ts
import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
// in edge handler
export default async function handler(req: Request) {
  const res = await client.generate(req)
  return new Response(await res.text())
}
```
sam: looks like overloads for generate expect either (input: string) or (opts: { input: string } | { request: Request })? we added a Request overload but the bundler TS path seems to pick a different signature.
sam: bundlers & module modes change how lib/dom types are resolved. edge target + moduleResolution:Bundler is new and can make 'Request' type ambiguous (node vs dom).
marco: ive seen this when lib ordering causes DOM Request to be different shape than our polyfilled one. try explicitly narrowing: `client.generate(req as unknown as any)` as a temporary workaround. ugly but unblocks.
lex: we should avoid encouraging any casts. better: fix overloads to prefer a single generic signature that accepts Request-like or string. e.g. `generate<T extends string|Request>(input: T): Promise<ResponseLike>` then inside runtime we detect. reduces overload ambiguity.
anya: i tried changing to a single generic in local fork and TS picked it fine, but run-time on edge failed because our type guards call `instanceof Request` which crashes in some edge envs (Request isn't same ctor).
devon: right — instanceof won't work across realms. prefer duck-typing: check for `.url` and `.method` or use `'request' in input` pattern.
sdk-bot: integration-tests/edge-repro failing — 7 errors in typecheck step. See CI job 4821.
marco: for immediate patch: 1) tighten overloads to a single signature that uses structural typing; 2) replace instanceof checks with duck typing; 3) update our tsconfig in sdk packages to include `lib: ["ES2020","DOM"]` and `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` in package devts to match consumers.
lex: also add a note in onboarding sample docs about recommended tsconfig for edge: bundle resolution, DOM lib, and avoid esModuleInterop assumptions. small snippet in docs will save time.
sam: question: should we change published types (major/minor bump) or add compatibility shim in runtime that accepts both node Request and DOM Request?
devon: we can do a minor release if it's just type/guard fixes and add tests. If we change public signatures to a single generic it might be semver-minor but safe.
anya: i'll open a PR with duck-typed guards + updated typedef and a small sample update. will include a failing test that CI can run in node + edge runners.
marco: nice. add an explicit note on unknown vs any: we should avoid widening to any; instead prefer `unknown` and then narrow where needed in SDK surface so downstream users don't lose type safety. but SDK internal helpers can use `any` cautiously.
lex: also lint rule suggestion: add a rule to disallow `instanceof Request` in packages that target multi-realm runtimes.
anya: pinging @devex to review sample patch once i open PR. will add repro in /examples/edge-typing.
devon: thx — if you need me to tweak CI to run a fast edge-typecheck job, I can add it.
anya: thanks all :raised_hands: will post PR link shortly.
sdk-bot: created ticket RW-8712 for tracking and assigned to @anya.
